Essay on the Origin of "Settle Colonial Theory" - A white Australian Dude from Stanford?!?!

Do you guys actually know where the term and conept of "settler colonial"  really originated?  Because it's not Fanon.  The term floated around for 20+ years without a formal academic instantiation.  When I was in college in the 90's (at SF State, a VERY "progressive" race conscious school) it wasn't very popular early on, people mostly took it from Sakai (which had died out by the early 1990's).

The academic establishment had rejected Sakai and there was a huge rift in the Fanonite intellectuals about it as well.  The consensus was that it wasn't going to work. 

The term was launched back into the limelight by Patrick Wolfe, a white Australian Harvard and Standford educated PhD who originally used in a series of articles.  Because of the response, his publisher at the time requested he change to the term "settlers" in his later books.  This was in the late 90's.  Then the corporate NGO floodgates, permeation into human resources social science, and it's general polarization occurred. 

That was how it happened, and since then leftist academy has been pretending it was some deep baked in concept to Fanonism (which it was NOT).  

So let it sink in, "Settler Colonial" is a term and concept primarily popularized by a white god damn Australian Ivy league MF who got his degree from the London School of Economics.  

The irony of this is beyond mention, and it has not been mentioned.  😂
